problem: Light Emitting Diode fails to illuminate when triggered by GPIO pin.
causes: Reversed polarity (anode connected to GND, cathode to positive)
Missing or wrong current-limiting resistor value
Wrong GPIO pin configured in sketch or pin declared as INPUT mode instead of OUTPUT
Blown LED diode junction caused by prior over-voltage
tests_to_perform: Diode mode multimeter check across LED leads (forward voltage ~1.8V - 2.2V)
Measure DC voltage on output pin during HIGH state (should be 5V or 3.3V)
Verify continuity of series current-limiting resistor
steps: Check LED orientation: the longer lead (anode) must connect towards the positive GPIO pin, and the flat edge side (cathode) towards ground.
Inspect code: verify pinMode(pin, OUTPUT) is declared in setup() and digitalWrite(pin, HIGH) is executed.
Check resistor value: ensure a 220Ω to 330Ω resistor is connected in series with the LED.
Swap LED: if wiring and code are correct, test with a fresh LED in case the junction was blown.

problem: Cellular SIM800L / SIM900 module fails to register on network or AT commands timeout.
causes: Insufficient current supply (GSM requires 2A burst current during network search)
Voltage level mismatch on RX/TX serial pins (5V logic connected directly to 3.3V RX)
TX and RX serial lines swapped with microcontroller pins
Invalid or unseated micro-SIM card (2G network required)
tests_to_perform: Measure VCC rail during power-up with multimeter to check for dips below 3.7V
Inspect Netlight LED blink pattern (fast blink = searching, 3s blink = registered)
Send basic 'AT' test command over Serial Monitor at 9600 baud
steps: Power Supply Check: do not power GSM from Arduino 5V pin. Provide external 3.7V - 4.2V 2A power source (e.g. LM2596 buck converter or Li-Ion battery).
Common Ground: connect the ground pin of the external GSM power supply to the microcontroller GND pin.
Serial Pin Verification: connect Arduino TX to GSM RX via voltage divider (1k/2k) and Arduino RX to GSM TX.
Baud Rate: ensure SoftwareSerial baud rate matches module default (typically 9600 baud).

symptom: HC-SR04 reads 0cm or out of range
problem: Ultrasonic distance sensor returns constant 0cm, 400cm, or NaN distance values.
causes: Trigger and Echo pins reversed in breadboard wiring or software pin mapping
Sensor acoustic transducer obscured or held at an oblique angle relative to target surface
Missing voltage divider on Echo pin when interfaced with 3.3V microcontrollers (ESP32 / Pi)
tests_to_perform: Measure 5V VCC supply voltage at sensor pins
Check oscilloscope or logic analyzer pulse on Trig pin (should be 10us HIGH pulse)
steps: Wiring Check: confirm Trig pin connects to Digital 9 and Echo pin connects to Digital 10.
Target Orientation: place a flat cardboard target 10cm to 30cm directly in front of the sensor face.
Check Power: ensure sensor receives full 5.0V VCC supply.

symptom: Arduino or ESP32 resets repeatedly when motor starts
problem: Microcontroller undergoes brownout reset (BOR) whenever DC motor or servo actuates.
causes: Motor stall inrush current pulls VCC line below 4.3V brownout threshold
Absence of flyback diode or inductive kickback noise on shared power rails
Missing decoupling electrolytic capacitors near motor driver
tests_to_perform: Measure logic 5V rail with multimeter / scope during motor startup
Verify presence of 1N4007 flyback diode across motor terminals
steps: Separate Power Rails: use dedicated battery pack or external power supply for motors.
Shared Ground: connect motor battery GND to microcontroller GND.
Decoupling Capacitors: place a 100uF - 470uF electrolytic capacitor across motor power supply rail.
Flyback Diode: install 1N4007 diode across motor terminals (cathode to positive).

symptom: ESP32 Wi-Fi fails to connect to network
problem: ESP32 SoC repeatedly fails WiFi.begin() or drops connection during RF transmission.
causes: Weak USB power cable causing peak current voltage drop during Wi-Fi beacon bursts
2.4GHz Wi-Fi network credential mismatch or 5GHz SSID selection (ESP32 supports 2.4GHz only)
ADC2 pin conflict while Wi-Fi stack is actively transmitting
tests_to_perform: Check Serial Monitor log at 115200 baud for WiFi.status() error code
Verify Wi-Fi network operates on 2.4GHz ISM band
steps: Verify Network Band: ensure connecting to 2.4GHz Wi-Fi band (5GHz networks are unsupported).
Power Quality: power ESP32 via high-quality USB cable connected to 1A+ powered port.
Pin Selection: avoid using ADC2 pins (GPIO 0, 2, 4, 12, 13, 14, 15, 25, 26, 27) when Wi-Fi is active.
